questions.text: Tell me about a process you designed from scratch. How did you know it was working?
questions.rationale: Process design with a measurement instinct built into the story.

questions.text: Describe the most chaotic operational situation you have walked into. What did you stabilize first?
questions.rationale: Triage sequencing under chaos is the defining ops instinct.

questions.text: Walk me through a vendor selection you ran. What criteria mattered and what surprised you post-signature?
questions.rationale: Vendor management maturity, including the post-signature reality check.

questions.text: How do you document a process so it survives you leaving? Show me your approach.
questions.rationale: Documentation discipline against the bus-factor, testable at any level.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you automated something people insisted needed human judgment. How did you decide it did not?
questions.rationale: Automation judgment, including respect for the cases that genuinely need humans.

questions.text: Describe a cross-functional project you coordinated where you had no formal authority. How did you keep it moving?
questions.rationale: Influence without authority is the operator's permanent condition.

questions.text: What kind of operational problem do you find most satisfying to fix?
questions.rationale: Locates genuine operational energy: systems, people, tools, or firefighting.

questions.text: Tell me about a time a process you built started failing at higher volume. How did you catch it and what did you change?
questions.rationale: Scale-breakage detection tests monitoring instinct and redesign ability.

questions.text: How do you decide between fixing a process and killing it?
questions.rationale: Kill discipline against sunk-cost attachment; the operator's hardest call.

questions.text: Describe your experience with operational metrics. Which one did you retire because it drove the wrong behavior?
questions.rationale: Metric side-effect awareness separates thoughtful operators from measurement maximalists.

questions.text: Tell me about implementing a tool the team resisted. How did adoption actually happen?
questions.rationale: Change management ground truth, past the rollout announcement.

questions.text: Walk me through your approach to writing a runbook for something only you know how to do.
questions.rationale: Knowledge transfer craft, concretely evidenced.

questions.text: Describe a time you found significant savings without cutting quality. Where did you look?
questions.rationale: Cost-quality tradeoff sophistication with a real find attached.

questions.text: How do you handle a stakeholder who keeps bypassing the process you built?
questions.rationale: Tests whether the response is enforcement, redesign, or inquiry; each says something.

questions.text: Tell me about a compliance or safety requirement you had to operationalize. How did you make it stick without resentment?
questions.rationale: Mandatory-process design with human factors accounted for.

questions.text: What is your project management approach when half the team is skeptical the project matters?
questions.rationale: Meaning-making as a project skill, not just scheduling.

questions.text: Describe an inventory, logistics, or capacity planning problem you solved. Walk me through your math.
questions.rationale: Quantitative ops fluency, checkable through the actual arithmetic.

questions.text: Tell me about the best operations culture you have worked in. What norms made it good?
questions.rationale: Culture pattern recognition from lived experience.

questions.text: How do you run a retrospective after an operational failure? What do you do with what you learn?
questions.rationale: Learning-loop craft; the follow-through half is where most retros die.

questions.text: Walk me through a quarter where you had to deliver with a materially reduced budget. What went and what stayed?
questions.rationale: Constraint prioritization with named sacrifices; realistic senior scenario.

questions.text: What does operational excellence mean to you, in one concrete example rather than a definition?
questions.rationale: Forces specificity where the term usually invites platitudes.

questions.text: Tell me about coordinating with a remote or offshore team. What broke first and how did you fix it?
questions.rationale: Distributed coordination failure modes, evidenced through experience.

questions.text: Describe your escalation philosophy. When do you wake someone up versus wait until morning?
questions.rationale: Escalation calibration reveals judgment about severity and respect for people.

questions.text: How do you keep routine operational work from consuming the time needed for improvement work?
questions.rationale: The run-versus-improve tension is the operator's permanent scheduling problem.

questions.text: As an ops lead, tell me about building a team's capacity plan. How did you handle the gap between plan and reality?
questions.rationale: Capacity leadership with a reality-gap probe testing adaptive management.

questions.text: Tell me about a direct report who was drowning in their queue. What did you actually do?
questions.rationale: People leadership in an overload scenario; actions over sentiments.

questions.text: What would you audit first if you joined our operations team tomorrow?
questions.rationale: Preparation plus diagnostic instinct applied to this company specifically.

questions.text: Describe your experience with SLAs. Tell me about one you renegotiated and why.
questions.rationale: SLA fluency including the maturity to renegotiate unrealistic commitments.

questions.text: Walk me through a workflow you mapped end to end. What did the map reveal that surprised people?
questions.rationale: Process mapping craft with a discovery payoff that indicates real depth.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were the calm one in an operational crisis. What were you doing internally?
questions.rationale: Composure under pressure, probed for the internal mechanics rather than the image.
